name: Charles Spurrier Mason
bio: The man with whom Alfred Taylor went through a marriage ceremony in 1893 - Taylor in a wedding dress as the bride, Mason as the bridegroom, an exchange of rings and a wedding breakfast afterwards. Charles Parker gave the ceremony in evidence at the Old Bailey in April 1895; Pierre Louys had reported it to Andre Gide at the time as 'a marriage - a real marriage - between two of them'. Wilde wrote to him from Worthing in August 1894 asking after 'poor Alfred' following the Fitzroy Street raid, and joking, 'I hope marriage has not made you too serious?'
bio_note: Dates 1868-1940 from the Complete Letters editors (p. 603 n. 2), who also note Croft-Cooke's suggestion that the marriage was genuine; McKenna calls him 'a twenty-five-year-old male prostitute' at the time of the ceremony, which is consistent with those dates.
